newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson pleased with Q2 performance. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson pleased with Q2 performance. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said Tuesday it was pleased with its second quarter performance.
Dayton Hudson said it earned $130 million, or $0.54 a share, during the second quarter ended August 2, versus $101 million, or $0.42 a share, during the same period a year ago.
This year's results included an $11 million, or $0.05 a share, charge for the redemption of debt. Minus the charge, Dayton Hudson earned $0.59 a share.
Street analysts had expected the company to earn $0.55 a share, according to First Call.

"We are pleased with our overall financial performance in the second quarter and year to date," Bob Ulrich, Dayton Hudson chairman and chief executive, said in a statement. "All three divisions continued to contribute to our improvement in earnings in the second quarter."
Revenues rose 9 percent in the quarter to $6.29 billion.

The Target division's pre-tax profit rose 14 percent to $274 million. Target's total revenues increased 14 percent and same-store revenues were up 6 percent. The gross margin rate fell due to higher markdowns, and the operating expense rate was flat compared with last year.

The Mervyn division's pre-tax profit was up 4 percent in second quarter to $58 million. Revenues fell 5 percent (corrects from "rose 5 percent"), primarily reflecting closed stores, while comparable-store revenues increased 2 percent. Mervyn's gross margin rate fell due to higher markdowns, while the operating expense rate improved due to lower store expenses and headquarters costs.

At the Department Store Division, pre-tax profit was $33 million versus $12 million in 1996. Total revenues rose 1 percent, and comparable-store revenues fell 1 percent. The division's gross margin rate increased, partially due to higher markup, and the operating expense rate improved significantly due to reductions in store expense and lower marketing costs.
